strength_level_weight.description: Weighting of STR, relative to the INT and VIT weights, when a stat point is allocated during level up.  For reasons known only to the original game devs, STR/INT/VIT follow different rules from other stats (ATK etc.). First, a certain number of stat points are allocated, minimum of 9 plus a random bonus. Then, point by point, each is assigned to one of the three stats, using an additional random roll compared against those weights.  Although the weights have very similar values in the game data to the other `_level` fields, and look like a % growth, their absolute values don't mean anything, they are just relative to each other.

model_set.description: Identifies a family of similar NPCs used for loading models/skeletons.  Although the actual value does tend to group together monsters with the same model--such as Shadow Panther and Blood Panther, or Buffaloo and Buffamoo--this tends to act more like a general "model type" and the exact value does not really matter so much as the range in which it falls: - All values between 48-253 treat the `model` as an index starting from 0x3128, the first `rom:/mons` entry, i.e. a monster model. - Other values treat the `model` as an index starting from 0x03A5, the first `rom:/chr` entry, i.e. a character. This includes actual characters but also inanimate objects like signs and furniture, which also happen to appear in the "character" list, but have values >= 254 for this field which triggers special behavior.  An additional property is that when a monster is spawned, a value of 0 causes the model to load with different parameters, probably as static rather than animated, since it largely applies to furniture and other inanimate objects. This _only_ applies to monster spawns; character spawns are done in an entirely different place and always use animated models.  These ranges are hard-coded in the game, and no evidence has been found that the value within the range makes any difference. Thus: - Major characters (non monsters) can have any value below 48, usually zero. Non-zero values (Blossom = 16) might indicate they can also be spawned as a "monster" in some event. - Monsters can have any value between 48 and 253. - Static objects usually have a value of 0, except those with values >= 254 which have special (hard-coded) behavior; don't use the high range unless you know what you're doing.

sight_range.description: How far the actor can see, i.e. aggro distance along the `sight_arc`. Works similarly to the `hit_range` but applied to their vision and not their attacks.

sight_arc.description: The actor's vision code or field of view, where 65536 = 360 degrees. Party members inside this arc and within the `sight_range` will cause aggro.

model.description: Index of the model asset, which is added to the model set offset (0x03A5 for characters, 0x3128 for monsters) to get the asset ID for the actor model. The value `0` is a real model; `-1` means no model.  While the manifest lists names with `.bfres` extension, which is a Nintendo archive format used with Switch, on PC these are a different, custom format containing similar data (geometry, skeleton, textures, etc.).  In a dump of the main bundle, these are the assets named `NPC_*.model` (characters), `BM_*.model` or `M_*.model` (monsters).

animation_set.description: Index of the first skeletal animation asset, which is always added to offset 0x3128 to get the asset ID for the actor's animations.  Only monster animation sets (`M_` and `BM_` files) exist as assets; unlike `model`, there is no separate category for human characters. The value `-1` means no animation, and most characters use that value, except one, which can also spawn as a monster. A value of `0` would point to a real animation.  These are both listed and dumped as `.bfskl` files, but actually appear to be `.bfres` containers each with only a single animation and no other data.

attack_set.description: Index offset of the attack set used by this actor.  Although not confirmed by decompilation, this is most likely added to 0x00F3 (beginning of the `rom:/as` entries) to get the asset ID, which for monsters will typically land on an `as_atk_mb_*` or `as_atk_m_*` file. For example, Orc has value 0x196, which adds up to 0x289, the ID of the first monster attack, `as_atk_m_00_00.bin`.  Characters always have 0 in this field unless they can also spawn as monsters.

ridden_attack_1.description: Index of the primary attack to perform when ridden by the player.  This is likely applied as an offset to the entry identified by `attack_set`. For example, if the first attack is `as_atk_m_06_00.bin`, and the value of this field is 0x7, then the attack used will be `as_atk_m_06_07.bin`.  Note that different NPCs do not have equal numbers of attack scripts. The value used for this field must be valid for the specific NPC and only has meaning for that NPC.

ridden_attack_1_alt.description: Alternate version of the primary mounted attack, applied when thrown (?). Usually the same as `ridden_attack_1`.

ridden_attack_2.description: Index of the secondary attack to perform when ridden by the player.  See `ridden_attack_1` for implementation details.

evs.description: Effort Values for this monster, named after the Pokemon concept. Low to high bytes are HP, STR, INT, VIT.  Tamed monsters initially have 50 points to distribute among the four stats, which ultimately become percentage bonuses, with HP values counting as double. When the player kills a monster of this type, with a tamed monster in his/her party, then that tamed monster will gain these points as percentage bonuses, until all 50 points have been assigned.  For example, if the player, with a tamed monster in the party, kills 25 Buffaloos (EV: +1 STR) and 25 Ants (EV: +1 HP) then the tamed monster ends up with a permanent bonus of +25% STR and +50% HP, and no more points can be assigned with additional kills.  Most of the time, regular monsters will provide +1 or +2 to a single stat. +3 or higher in a single stat, or non-zero values in multiple stats, are comparatively rare, although they are perfectly legal.
